chapter: Chicago radio, Whiteman and courting Mildred
title: Ben Bernie at the College Inn; Whiteman hears him
summary: He works with Ben Bernie's band at the Sherman's College Inn doing solos; Whiteman hears him play 'In a Mist' alone and hires him for NBC.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: And I never went back to Minneapolis. And, from that -- I don't know I was around there and I did some things with Ben Bernie, was -- so when he went in the College Inn, I went in with him, with Dick Stabile and all these people that was with Ben Bernie.
Yeah. What did you think of Dick Stabile.
All I did was solos. I'd work with the band, but I did -- I'd push the marimba around during -- play like " between sets. And then I'd Gollywog's, Cakewalk and --
Oh, I see.
" Prelude in C-Sharp -- or four-timer hammer things --
Yeah.
And Whiteman came in one night. You know,
and they had a big party and they'd been drinking and I didn't know him. I knew who he was --
Yeah.
-- but I didn't know he was there, I was playing like to the side of the dancehall, if you can remember the Sherman --
Yeah.
-- and he was sitting over there, straight in front of where the band plays.
Yeah.
So I played In a Mist -- and he flipped over it. I played it all alone.
Yeah.
So, when I moved back headwaiter came over and said, Mr. Whiteman wants to see you. Well I didn't think it was Paul Whiteman, I didn't think. I just -- somebody at a table, so I went over --
Yeah.
-- and I recognized him, and I nearly fainted. So, he put me to work at NBC. With Jules [Hermebol] HERMEBOL.
Well, what did he say to you?
Huh?
What did he say to you?
He said, 'that's wonderful playing, well who -- I mean -- I never heard anybody play like that,' he said.

I never heard anybody play like that. And then I played a couple of little pop tunes, and then I -- like four-hammers, then I -- I suppose you'd say in those days, I'd jazz up the choruses, play jazz on a couple of choruses, you know?
Yeah, yeah.

And, he said, 'I'm the musical director, gonna be musical director, he was working town, I guess, at that time. So they put me on with Jules Hermebol, I remember we had a five piece band and we worked all day.
